test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Train A, running at a speed of 32 km/hr, takes 33 seconds to completely cross train B, running at 28 km/hr in the opposite direction. The length of train B is 1.5 times the length of train A. Train B crosses a bridge completely in 54 seconds. What is the length of the bridge (in m)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in **opposite direction** = 32 + 28 = 60 km/hr = 60 × (5/18) = 50/3 m/s.

Total distance (LA + LB) = Speed × Time = (50/3) × 33 = 550 m.

Since LB = 1.5 LA, Total = 2.5 LA = 550 ⇒ LA = 220 m and **LB = 330 m**.

Distance covered by B in 54s = (28 × 5/18) × 54 = 420 m.

Length of Bridge = Total Distance − LB = 420 − 330 = 90 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db0dda5bab406a042212005e966200c7b66d980908cbdd177ecb34c1aac7d272.png] 

**Given:** SpeedA = 32 km/hr, SpeedB = 28 km/hr, Time꜀ᵣₒₛₛᵢₙg = 33 s, LB = 1.5 LA, Timebᵣᵢdgₑ = 54 s.

**Formula:** Relative Speed (Opposite) = S₁ + S₂ | Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Relative Speed = (32 + 28) × 5/18 = 60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/s

⇒ LA + LB = (50/3) × 33 = 550 m

⇒ LA + 1.5 LA = 550 ⇒ 2.5 LA = 550 ⇒ LA = 220 m

⇒ Length of **Train B** (LB) = 1.5 × 220 = 330 m

⇒ Speed of Train B in m/s = 28 × 5/18 = 70/9 m/s

⇒ Total distance (Train B + Bridge) = (70/9) × 54 = 420 m

⇒ Length of Bridge = 420 − 330 = 90 m

**∴ The correct answer is 90 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂. In the same direction, it is |S₁ − S₂|.

Crossing Objects

When a train crosses a bridge or another train, the total distance covered is the sum of their lengths (L₁ + L₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p
